label: What-If Scenarios
description: Turns broad research into a sharp what if condition, revealing everyday consequences, affected groups, risks, values, and discussable speculative scenarios.

text_output_forms.primary_template: condition card, everyday vignette, stakeholder impact table, and open questions

required_blocks.title: What changes?
required_blocks.purpose: State one precise what-if condition and its new rule.

required_blocks.title: An ordinary day under this rule
required_blocks.purpose: Use a short, situated vignette rather than a general answer.

required_blocks.title: Questions that resist closure
required_blocks.purpose: Keep the premise discussable instead of resolving it.

text_output_forms.presentation_rule: Use actual text blocks and a table, never Markdown table syntax. Localize labels to the response language.

theory_mapping.source_notes: 思辨设计tools-3.pdf pages 7-8, What-Ifs / 假设情境.

model_constraints: Convert the source topic into one sharp 'What if...' condition.
Make the changed condition concrete enough to generate everyday consequences.
Identify who benefits, who is harmed, and what new rule, service, object, or unfairness may appear.
Avoid broad future hype; ground the scenario in bodily, social, labor, consumption, or governance changes.
For text outputs, return the package text_blocks sequence; do not collapse the result into a single explanatory essay or Markdown table.

recommendation.reason: What-If works best as a first written scenario seed: it compresses a broad issue into one sharp changed condition before any artifact or image is made.
best_when: The input topic is broad, abstract, or ethically difficult.
The user needs a discussable premise before choosing objects, scenes, or visual evidence.
The next step is stakeholder discussion, risk mapping, or value debate.

image: image prompt for the most concrete consequence
multimodal: semantic summary of the world rule

avoid: standalone image without the what-if premise

warnings: Start with text unless the input already contains a concrete scene or object to visualize.
